principles.rule: Follow the Dependency Rule: source code dependencies point only inward, toward higher-level policy. Inner layers must not know anything about outer layers.
checks: business rules import no frameworks
no DB/UI/web types in entities or use cases
data formats of outer layers never leak inward

principles.rule: Single Responsibility: each module is responsible to exactly one actor/stakeholder, i.e. has one reason to change.
checks: no class mixing concerns of different actors
split modules that change for different reasons

principles.rule: Open-Closed: add new behavior by adding code, not by modifying existing working code. Protect higher-level components from changes in lower-level ones.
checks: new features via extension points/polymorphism
directional control via interfaces

principles.rule: Liskov Substitution: subtypes must be substitutable for their base types without special-casing.
checks: no type checks/instanceof branching to handle a subtype
subtypes honor base contracts

principles.rule: Interface Segregation: do not depend on things you do not use. Prefer narrow, client-specific interfaces over fat ones.
checks: interfaces expose only methods the client needs
no forced dependency on unused members

principles.rule: Dependency Inversion: depend on abstractions, not concretions. Stable, high-level policy must not reference volatile concrete classes; invert via interfaces.
checks: high-level modules import interfaces only
concrete implementations injected at the boundary (Main)

principles.rule: No cyclic dependencies between components. Break cycles with DIP or by extracting a new component.
checks: component dependency graph is a DAG

principles.rule: Depend in the direction of stability and abstraction: stable components are abstract (policy); unstable components are concrete (details).
checks: volatile code does not sit at the stable core
abstractions live in stable components

principles.rule: Treat database, web, and frameworks as details/plugins. Keep them out of the business core and defer/isolate these decisions as long as possible.
checks: no ORM/HTTP/framework imports in entities or use cases
persistence behind a gateway interface
framework usage isolated at the edge

principles.rule: Draw architectural boundaries between things that change for different reasons or at different rates; cross boundaries only through well-defined interfaces.
checks: clear ports/adapters at boundaries
no business logic in controllers/presenters

principles.rule: Make the structure scream the application's purpose, not the framework. Prefer package-by-feature/component over package-by-layer.
checks: top-level packages reflect domain, not tech
encapsulation enforced via visibility modifiers

principles.rule: Use the Humble Object pattern: separate hard-to-test code (views, I/O) from testable logic (presenters, interactors).
checks: views contain no logic
logic testable without GUI/DB

principles.rule: A good architecture maximizes the number of decisions NOT made (keep options open) and minimizes the human effort to build and maintain the system.
checks: key infrastructure choices are deferrable and reversible
